calls.reason: An opinion-framed forecast with no deadline. The only evidence is Microsoft's withdrawal from the Nscale Loughton site, and Nscale says it remains committed, so permanent noncompletion of many deals is not shown.
Mixed: CoreWeave's 10-K shows interest expense tripling, but Microsoft gave about 67% of its revenue, undercutting the 'AI startups' framing. CBRE shows the pipeline dipped while capacity grew 36%.
'At some point' sets no deadline. NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 10-Q shows Data Center revenue up 117% year on year, so no decline has happened, but growth cannot rule out an eventual one.

Anthropic's audited S-1 shows about $5.0B revenue for 2023–2025, but only about $12.7B in compute plus personnel costs. Reaching $25B would need about $12B in 2022, implausible next to roughly $0.5B in 2023.
Largely opinion and rhetoric. The trials conflict: METR found a 19% slowdown in early 2025 but later saw some speedup, and a Google RCT found tasks about 21% faster. Learning harm isn't established.

The core gigawatt point is the speaker's own unsuccessful search, with no operating records either way. Side clauses lean wrong (a 100MW design in 2011, OpenAI's roughly $40B cash), but the main point is unsettled.
